content: Indication-specific dosing for vinpocetine (Intelecitol) is typically 5-10 mg taken orally three times daily (TID) with food. This medication is known to increase cerebral blood flow and metabolism, provide anticonvulsant effects, enhance cognition, offer neuroprotection, and exhibit antioxidant properties. It also promotes cerebral vasodilation. Some clinical studies suggest that vinpocetine may have prophylactic effects in ischemic stroke and cognitive improvement. However, it has not been shown to be beneficial in Alzheimer’s disease. Vinpocetine is sold as a legal pharmaceutical product in Japan, Europe, and Mexico. Interactions with certain medications, such as alprazolam, chlordiazepoxide, clonazepam, clorazepate, diazepam, estazolam, flurazepam, loprazolam, lorazepam, lormetazepam, midazolam, oxazepam, quazepam, temazepam, and triazolam, have been observed. These drugs increase the effects of vinpocetine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of these interactions is considered minor or unknown. However, these interactions may result in desirable effects, such as enhanced memory improvement, as suggested by preliminary trials. Adverse effects associated with vinpocetine include nausea, dizziness, insomnia, drowsiness, dry mouth, transient hypotension, transient tachycardia, pressure-type headaches, and facial flushing. Prolonged use may lead to slight reductions in both systolic and diastolic blood pressure, as well as blood glucose levels. Contraindications for vinpocetine include hypersensitivity to vinpocetine or other vinca alkaloids, incomplete homeostasis following cerebral hemorrhage, pregnancy, lactation, patients under 18 years of age, hemophilia, heart problems, or low blood pressure. Patients on warfarin should have their INR levels monitored closely. Vinpocetine is classified under Pregnancy Category: Avoid. It should not be used during pregnancy or lactation.
